newsitem.title: FRANCE: French N-train on way to Germany, Greenpeace says.
newsitem.headline: French N-train on way to Germany, Greenpeace says.

text.p: Greenpeace anti-nuclear activists said on Tuesday a train carrying nuclear waste was on its way from western France to northern Germany but would not arrive there for another two weeks for security reasons.

Greenpeace spokeswoman Penelope Komites said the train, carrying two containers of nuclear waste processed at La Hague near the Channel port of Cherbourg, had left nearby Valognes on Monday night bound for the German depot at Gorleben.
A spokeswoman for the state COGEMA reprocessing plant declined to comment.

Komites said the Gorleben depot would not be able to handle the shipment until March 3 or 4 because heavy security measures needed to prevent protests along the train's route in Germany were not yet in place.

The medium-term nuclear depot and planned long-term dump at Gorleben is a favourite target of the anti-nuclear movement and last year more than 19,000 police and border guards were called in to ensure a shipment reached the plant safely.

Komites said the train from La Hague would have to stop for several days before entering Germany. It could stop either in the French port of Dunkerque at the terminal of the firm Nuclear Transport Ltd or at the French nuclear plant of Catenon near the Luxembourg border.
She said transport documents obtained by Greenpeace led her to believe it would stop in Dunkerque.
German anti-nuclear activists argue that it is too dangerous to transport heavy nuclear waste shipments on rails and bridges which have not been built to take the strain of such a weight.
New fears about nuclear shipments were sparked nearly two weeks ago when a train carrying nuclear waste through eastern France was derailed, although officials said there was no radiation leak.
